correctness.rationale: The cited Kania–Kochanek local Steinhaus norm-germ characterization is the correct equivalence. In a strictly convex real normed block of dimension ≥2, distinct u,v always have unequal small norm increments: choose perturbation along u if noncollinear, opposite sign for opposing collinear rays, a noncollinear direction with strict triangle inequality for unequal same-direction scalars, and handle zero separately. In the ℓ1-sum each coordinate increment adds exactly, so differing high-dimensional block yields separation; if all such coordinates coincide and at most one real scalar block remains, equality of unit norms forces opposite scalar entries and a small perturbation separates them. With two scalar blocks, (1/3,2/3) vs (2/3,1/3), zero elsewhere, have identical norm germs for ‖h‖<1/3, proving sharp necessity. For complex L1 over arbitrary measure, A={|f−g|>1/m} has 0<µ(A)<∞; at each point the complex-plane increment lemma offers an arbitrarily small rational complex q separating increments. Countable measurable sign sets cover A; selecting one with positive measure gives h=q 1_B with arbitrarily small L1 norm and strictly nonzero total increment. Covers nonσfinite measures because A has finite measure; no numerical check needed.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Both have different hypotheses: atomless real/Bochner result does not cover arbitrarily atomic complex scalar L1; p>1 result does not imply the precise ℓ1 endpoint under strictly convex summands.

value.rationale: The ℓ1 endpoint of permanence is a motivated sharp structural boundary: a complete arbitrary-index characterization in terms of the NUMBER of 1D real summands, not an unmotivated isolated example. It yields a natural and potentially useful contrast between real and complex scalar L1 with arbitrarily many atoms. A general ℓp (1<p<∞) preservation theorem and atomless Bochner L1 coverage do not give this sharp endpoint classification.
